title: Trang Cake 2026 — Buttery Ring Cake & Where to Buy It | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: A guide to Trang cake, the buttery ring-shaped sponge of southern Thailand. Top shops from Khuk Ming in Lamphura to Rot Loet, Tha Pap and Kanittha — with real prices, neighborhoods, and how to pick the right box.
keywords: Trang cake, cake from Trang, ring cake Thailand, Trang souvenirs, Khuk Ming cake, Tha Pap cake
intro: Come to Trang and leave without a box of cake, and locals will tell you that you never really arrived. Trang cake is a dense, springy sponge with a hole through the middle, fragrant with butter and egg and never cloyingly sweet. Southerners have been passing it down as a gift for generations. We've rounded up the shops that are actually open right now, what they cost, where to find them, and how to pick a box you'll actually enjoy.

blocks.html: Trang cake isn't the light, fluffy sponge you might picture. It's dense and springy, and when you slice it you can see the fine pockets running through the middle of each piece — perfect with a hot coffee in the morning. It traces back to the egg cakes of Hainanese Chinese settlers who put down roots in Trang more than a century ago, then slowly adjusted the recipe into the cake people eat today. What sets it apart is the clear butter-and-egg aroma, the well-judged sweetness, and the fact that many shops still make it by hand, with no baking powder or preservatives.

blocks.text: Why Trang cake has a hole in the middle

blocks.html: The hole in the middle isn't there to look pretty. It comes from a round baking tin with a central tube that lets the heat reach every part of the batter, so the inside cooks evenly all the way through without leaning on much baking powder. Out comes a round cake with a hole, dense but still moist — not the kind that dries out and sticks in your throat. That shape is the giveaway: people spot it and know straight away it's a Trang cake.

blocks.title: Know before you buy
blocks.html: Many of the original Trang cake shops skip preservatives, so the cake keeps for about 4–5 days at room temperature. If you're carrying it a long way or storing it longer, keep it in the fridge and give it a short blast in the microwave before eating — it comes back soft and fragrant, just like fresh.

blocks.text: Trang cake shops people actually carry home

blocks.html: We've ordered these starting with the original shop and the ones locals and visitors mention most often. Prices are rough ranges and may shift with box size and flavor. It's worth calling ahead to check stock and opening hours, since some flavors are made fresh each day and sell out fast.

items.name: Khuk Ming Cake (Lamphura)
items.blurb: The real original Trang cake, around for more than 60 years. It sits on Phetkasem Road in the Lamphura area. The draw is that it's handmade, with no baking powder and no preservatives — dense crumb, strong egg aroma. There's an original flavor, butter, coffee, and an orange cream-filled roll cake that plenty of people make the trip just to buy.
items.meta: Lamphura, on Phetkasem Road · open roughly 6:00–19:00
items.price: From the low tens to under ฿100 per small box

items.name: Rot Loet Cake
items.blurb: An in-town shop on Soi Sathani, near Trang railway station. Reviewers agree the crumb is soft with a hint of moisture, never dry and throat-sticking, with just-right sweetness. The flavors people talk about are the three-flavor cake and the fruit cake packed dense with dried fruit. Open from morning to evening, so it's an easy stop before your train.
items.meta: Soi Sathani, near Trang railway station · open roughly 6:00–21:00
items.price: Fruit cake ฿130 small box / ฿190 large box

items.name: Tha Pap Cake
items.blurb: A bakery and souvenir shop known across the whole province. The standout is the young-coconut-topped cake — soft, fragrant, and made fresh daily. Alongside several Trang cake flavors, it stocks other local souvenirs in one place, so it suits anyone who wants to get all their shopping done in a single stop.
items.meta: In Trang town · storefront plus online orders
items.price: About ฿120–220 per box depending on flavor

items.name: Kanittha Cake
items.blurb: A Trang souvenir brand that doubles as a rest stop and souvenir hub. There's vanilla, pandan and golden-threads (foi thong) cake, plus steamed dumplings and tao so pastries. Easy parking, restrooms on site — a handy stop along the way before you leave Trang.
items.meta: Na Yong side / edge of town · parking available

items.name: Kui Li Cake
items.blurb: Another long-running shop that Trang locals know by name. The crumb is the traditional style, buttery and fragrant, and the price is easy on the wallet — good for buying several boxes to hand out. If you want the homey, old-school flavor your parents' generation grew up on, this one delivers.

items.name: Green House Cake
items.blurb: In town for over 10 years, known for nicely designed birthday cakes and more modern bakery items. If you're after a decorated cake or a celebration cake rather than the traditional souvenir style, this shop is the better fit.

items.name: Trang cake at markets / local souvenir shops
items.blurb: If you'd rather not pin yourself to one shop, walking the fresh markets and souvenir stores in town turns up Trang cake from several makers sold side by side. Taste and compare, then pick the one you like best. The upside is you can buy a single piece before committing to a big box.
items.meta: Markets and souvenir shops in town

blocks.text: Which flavor to buy first on a first visit

items: Butter (original) — the base flavor where the butter and egg come through clearest. If you want to know what real Trang cake tastes like, start here.
Coffee — a light coffee aroma that cuts the richness, good for anyone who doesn't like things too sweet.
Orange cream-filled roll cake — the Khuk Ming specialty, with a hint of orange and sweet, rich cream. It's a flavor lots of people keep coming back for.
Young coconut topping — the Tha Pap specialty, with young coconut added for extra juiciness — easier to keep eating than the plain version.
Fruit cake — a dense, drier crumb packed with dried fruit that keeps longer, so it's good for carrying a long way.

blocks.text: Buying it as a gift and getting a good box

items: Always check the production and expiry dates first. Shops that skip preservatives keep for a shorter time — around 4–5 days at room temperature.
If you're carrying it on a flight or traveling far, choose the fruit cake or a drier-crumbed cake that keeps longer.
For popular flavors like the orange roll or young-coconut topping, call to reserve ahead, since they're made fresh daily and sell out fast.
Buying several boxes? Ask about a bulk price — some shops give a discount on larger orders.

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: Trang cake is a lot denser than a Western-style sponge, so if you love light, airy cake it might feel a touch heavy. It's best with a hot coffee or tea. And don't buy a lot at once if you've never had it — taste a piece first, then commit to the big box.

faq.q: How is Trang cake different from a regular cake?
faq.a: Trang cake has a dense, springy crumb and a hole through the middle from a tube baking tin. It's clearly fragrant with butter and egg, the sweetness is well judged, and many of the original shops make it by hand with no baking powder or preservatives — unlike the light, fluffy Western-style sponge.

faq.q: Which Trang cake shop is the original?
faq.a: Khuk Ming in Lamphura is considered the original, around in Trang for more than 60 years. In town, the names people mention most are Rot Loet near the railway station and Tha Pap, which is known for its young-coconut topping.

faq.q: How long does Trang cake keep?
faq.a: Shops that skip preservatives keep for about 4–5 days at room temperature, and longer in the fridge. We'd give it a short blast in the microwave before eating to bring back the softness and aroma. The drier-crumbed fruit cake keeps longer and is better for carrying a long way.

faq.q: About how much does Trang cake cost?
faq.a: Small boxes start from the low tens up to around ฿130, with large boxes around ฿190–220 depending on the shop and flavor. Buying by the piece at a market runs about ฿10–25 each, so you can taste before you commit.

faq.q: Where's the most convenient place to buy Trang cake if you're short on time?
faq.a: If you're coming by train, Rot Loet on Soi Sathani is right by Trang railway station. If you're driving out of town, stop at Kanittha — it's a rest stop with easy parking and a full range of souvenirs in one place.
